raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

HiDream-O1-Image executes rotate-half RoPE separately for Q and K in all 36 transformer layers. At 2048×2048 and 50 CFG steps, the eager elementwise chain launches 57,600 kernels. Reusing the existing BF16-rounded RoPE kernel reduces this to 7,200 launches and lowers saved-request latency by **4.87–4.92%** in two independent paired rounds on B300.

- Main baseline: `4c7c775cf4adcbd2c7419d13b51ec838a17e559e`.
- Final tested PR head: `4b0f75d26a870d2401782545e1a2a4e173f752ee`.
- Before cleanup: `603193d7d31a91ddc7bb0bced66c37030fbd1991`.
- Checkpoint: `HiDream-ai/HiDream-O1-Image@0b0901d99f200389e138c61946af1185f5f49a13`.

## Modifications

- Reuse `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact` for contiguous CUDA BF16 Q/K. Its separate BF16 product and sum rounding matches the native eager expression; attention and normalization are unchanged.
- Reuse `BitExactFusionGate` for first-call equality checking, mismatch/exception disabling, and eager fallback. Unsupported layouts/dtypes retain the native path.
- Add four focused dispatch/fallback cases to the existing registered test and document this call site in the kernel README. The source diff contains no new kernel, option, cache or precision policy.

## Accuracy Tests

Final-source quality: **32 PNGs, 25 controlled PNG-byte and decoded-RGB comparisons exact**. This covers short/long prompts at lossless/exact/high, repeat/revisit, CFG1, TP2 and final generation without observer hooks. Each quality tier and TP topology is compared with its own main. Exact RGB implies PSNR = ∞, SSIM = 1, maximum pixel error = 0 for those controlled pairs. All 172 sampled actual Q/K comparisons pass `torch.equal`; the final path executes 7,200 fused calls per rank/request at CFG5, and 3,600 at CFG1. Both TP2 ranks verify and use the gate.

All **162 final-timing PNGs** and **10 final-profile PNGs** also match their main references exactly. The final scoped GPU suite passes **27 tests + 54 subtests**, with 126 unrelated tests deselected and no selected skips. It covers GQA, batch-specific tables, repeated changed inputs, input/V preservation, strided/FP32 fallback and forced mismatch disabling. Full-model batch>1 and FP32 support are not inferred from these attention fixtures.

These panels contain the actual final-source main/PR images at unchanged original pixel resolution, with matching prompts, seed, shape, steps and precision:

![HiDream short lossless, main and final](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-hidream-rope-evidence-20261104/short-main-final.png)

![HiDream long lossless, main and final](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-hidream-rope-evidence-20261104/long-main-final.png)

![HiDream short exact, main and final](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-hidream-rope-evidence-20261104/short-exact-main-final.png)

**vLLM-Omni control:** native commit `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`, same checkpoint/physical GPU/BF16/requests. Initial noise, token IDs, positions, mask semantics, timesteps and sigmas were checked. Its default `enforce_eager=False`, CuDNN attention and piecewise mask path remain enabled. Runtime observations found no installed regional modules, but one compiled Dynamo helper graph and 16 Inductor kernels. Native flow conversion and CFG arithmetic differ; the observed image difference is not attributed solely to one cause.

| Native main vs Omni | PSNR (dB) | SSIM | 28 dB / 0.95 gate | Qualified speed ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Short / repeat / revisit | 17.7348 | 0.80032 | Fail | — |
| Long | 17.9790 | 0.82432 | Fail | — |

All four failures are retained. Omni quality diagnostics used its native CPU placement and predate the controlled CPU65 timing. This PR claims a SGLang main-to-final gain; cross-framework quality did not qualify a latency ratio.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One **NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC**, driver 590.48.01; native SGLang, all components resident, BF16, 2048×2048, 50 steps, CFG5, CPU seed42, batch1/concurrency1, PNG compression0. Torch2.14.1+cu130 / Transformers5.19.0 / Diffusers0.37.0. The separate Omni environment uses Torch2.13.0+cu130 / Diffusers0.40.0; full inventories are attached. The task-owned GPU worker main thread is fixed to **CPU65 (GPU-local NUMA2)** before the first warmup in every main/pre/final engine; the original process affinity is restored afterward. This is a measurement control in the archived harness, not part of the PR. CPU identity and frequency are checked outside the timed interval; CPU/GPU frequency and power policies are unchanged. No observer hooks, RNG override, profiler, stage synchronization, torch.compile or BCG in formal timing.

Timer: native SDK `generate()` through completed PNG saving; output hashing is outside the timer. Eighteen fresh engines: `MM PP FF`, then `M P F F P M` twice. Each engine runs three warmup + six formal requests, retaining every sample. Each paired round has four samples per arm/contract (eight across both rounds).

| Contract | Round | Main E2E (s) | Final E2E (s) | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| short-lossless | 1 | 13.06402 | 12.42088 | 4.923% |
| short-lossless | 2 | 13.05527 | 12.41758 | 4.884% |
| long-lossless | 1 | 13.06939 | 12.42598 | 4.923% |
| long-lossless | 2 | 13.06729 | 12.42682 | 4.901% |
| short-exact | 1 | 13.05721 | 12.42192 | 4.865% |
| short-exact | 2 | 13.05510 | 12.41948 | 4.869% |

Each table entry averages the medians of its two corresponding engine sessions. Every repeated reduction exceeds 1.5% and measured A/A drift.

Cleanup removed redundant test assertions for unchanged behavior; production code is identical before/after cleanup. It was nevertheless independently retested:

| Contract | Main A/A | Pre A/A | Final A/A | Cleanup change, rounds1/2 | Cleanup noise bound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| short-lossless | 0.025% | 0.016% | 0.013% | +0.008%, -0.033% | 0.016% |
| long-lossless | 0.056% | 0.013% | 0.066% | -0.022%, -0.008% | 0.066% |
| short-exact | 0.030% | 0.015% | 0.039% | +0.010%, -0.035% | 0.039% |

Positive cleanup change means slower. All controlled v10 rounds meet the same A/A-based cleanup formula used in the original experiment. This full 18-engine run was preregistered after diagnosing a CPU-placement confound; it is not pooled with the earlier uncontrolled data. Every sample is retained and there is no threshold floor.

<details>
<summary>Earlier failed cleanup gates and the controlled CPU-placement diagnosis</summary>

The original mixed-contract v5 exact round2 failed its cleanup gate. An independent exact-only v7 confirmation also failed its first paired round. Their thresholds, all 270 generated images and raw samples remain unchanged:

| Original protocol | Exact round | Cleanup change | A/A bound | Original result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v5 mixed-contract | 1 | -0.182435% | 0.115631% | Pass |
| v5 mixed-contract | 2 | +0.133380% | 0.115631% | FAIL |
| v7 exact-only | 1 | +0.281331% | 0.250750% | FAIL |
| v7 exact-only | 2 | -0.114942% | 0.250750% | Pass |

The v7 four-round aggregate, including the original v5 rounds, was +0.029199%; this did not override its failed per-round criterion. The v7 protocol used three warmup plus six short-exact requests per engine, versus the mixed-contract v5/v10 warmup. Each protocol kept its arms symmetric.

Four fresh engines running the *same final source* then reproduced the fast/slow modes (36 exact PNGs). All 591 NVML samples during their measured request intervals showed the same SM 2032 MHz / memory 3996 MHz and no throttle flag. Fast processes mainly used CPU65/193, which motivated a bounded within-process experiment.

One loaded final-head engine alternated only its GPU-worker main-thread affinity between CPU65 and CPU70 in `A B B A`, then `B A A B`, with two requests per assignment. Both cores belong to GPU-local NUMA2; no code, model state, GPU setting or other-thread affinity changed:

| Same-process round | CPU65 E2E (s) | CPU70 E2E (s) | CPU70 extra (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 12.432397 | 12.466723 | 34.327 |
| 2 | 12.433825 | 12.467995 | 34.170 |

Request-end CPU-frequency readings were approximately 4.6 GHz on CPU65 and 2.3 GHz on CPU70. The 19 outputs were exact and the original affinity was restored. This demonstrates a repeatable CPU-placement confound of about 34 ms. The old v5/v7 runs did not record their CPUs, so individual old samples cannot be causally assigned to this factor. The underlying hardware/kernel frequency policy is not claimed to be diagnosed.

The final tables above use only the new v10 run, with *all three arms* fixed to CPU65 and the original 18-engine order, workload, timing interval and gate formulas. The plan, old failures, read-only telemetry and controlled experiment are in the raw archive. Pinning is neither a production-code change nor a separate performance PR.

</details>

| Contract | Arm | E2E p50 (s) | E2E p95 (s) | Serial requests/s | Peak reserved MiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| short-lossless | main | 13.05817 | 13.07460 | 0.07657 | 16334 |
| short-lossless | final | 12.42005 | 12.42473 | 0.08052 | 16370 |
| long-lossless | main | 13.07082 | 13.07524 | 0.07652 | 16334 |
| long-lossless | final | 12.42607 | 12.43449 | 0.08047 | 16370 |
| short-exact | main | 13.05576 | 13.06351 | 0.07659 | 16334 |
| short-exact | final | 12.42050 | 12.42729 | 0.08051 | 16370 |

The p95 values are descriptive for eight paired samples, not production tail estimates; reciprocal mean is serial saved-request rate, not concurrent HTTP throughput. Peak reserved memory changes from 16,334 to 16,370 MiB (+36 MiB).

| Arm (paired engines) | Fresh-engine initialization range (s) | Three-request warmup total range (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 21.455–27.095 | 41.286–41.304 |
| pre | 21.634–27.201 | 39.376–39.385 |
| final | 25.182–29.353 | 39.380–39.394 |

No graph capture occurs. Warmup includes the first-call gate/JIT costs. Separate synchronized, unprofiled stage measurements on the final source, also with CPU65 fixed:

| Prompt / lossless | Main denoise (s) | Final denoise (s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| short | 13.016338 | 12.373439 |
| long | 13.030954 | 12.385883 |

Independent full-request Torch traces on the final source and the same CPU65 control:

| Full 50-step denoise trace | Main | Final |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All denoise CUDA kernels | 131836 | 81436 |
| Summed denoise kernel time (ms) | 12861.851 | 12291.587 |
| GPU active interval union (ms) | 12809.910 | 12239.533 |
| RoPE kernel launches | 57600 | 7200 |
| RoPE kernel time (ms) | 637.064 | 69.152 |

The RoPE subtotal uses CPU-op attribution and half-Q/K shapes, excluding KV expansion/mask copies. Sequence lengths 4107/4125 are the negative/positive branches of the profiled short request. Net RoPE GPU-time saving is 567.912ms. Complete kernel groups, unmapped events and active interval unions are retained. Profile timings include instrumentation overhead and are not substituted for formal E2E results.

### Reproduction and scope

Download the [review package](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-hidream-rope-evidence-20261104/hidream-rope-review-evidence-v4.zip) for exact commands/configs, source bundles, final/failed reports, environment inventories and cleanup review. The [complete raw archive](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/releases/download/b300-hidream-rope-evidence-20261104/hidream-rope-evidence-v4.tar.xz) includes every saved image, input diagnostic, log and full trace, with a per-file SHA256 manifest. Use a new job name when replaying the archived workers; the README includes independent worker commands and the complete pairing protocol. No weights, traces or media enter the code diff.

Measured model scope: BF16 eager on one B300, with TP2 correctness checked separately. No new BCG support, cache, quantization, other resolution, concurrent serving, offload, compile or TP2 speed claim is made. Existing HiDream attention-splitting PR #45137 is a separate change and is not reproduced here.

## Checklist

- [x] Scoped pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.
- [x] Focused registered regression coverage and actual model quality tests pass.
- [x] Kernel documentation updated.
- [x] Final-source accuracy, repeated speed, cleanup and profile evidence included.
- [x] Complete diff reviewed and simplified within this optimization's scope.

Draft status leaves upstream CI/review outstanding; local B300 validation is not a claim that CI has passed.

detail.title: [Perf] diffusion: reuse bit-exact RoPE in HiDream-O1-Image

files.patch:
@@ -204,7 +204,7 @@ tensor copy at each residual site.
 | `try_fused_flux2_qkv_epilogue` | KDA (JIT CUDA) | bit-exact vs the selected BF16 chain | FLUX.2 QK RMSNorm + RoPE + joint QKV packing |
 | `try_fused_qwen_qkv_epilogue` | JIT CUDA | bit-exact vs the selected BF16 chain | Qwen-Image QK RMSNorm + RoPE + joint QKV writes; SM90+ |
 | `rmsnorm_cast_before_weight_rope_bitexact` | Triton | ATen-ordered RMSNorm plus exact BF16 rotate-half RoPE, MOSS-Image width 128 |
-| `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact` | Triton | bit-exact (elementwise only) |
+| `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact` | Triton | separate BF16 rounding after each product and the sum; HiDream-O1-Image reuses it for contiguous Q/K with first-call verification and eager fallback |
 | `fused_rope_rotate_half_fp32` | Triton | paired split-half Q/K RoPE with separately rounded FP32 products and sum before the FP16/BF16 cast; Anima verifies each new signature against eager |
 | `flux3_video_qknorm_rope` | Triton | bit-exact vs affine-free ``nn.RMSNorm`` (head dim 64) plus eager rotate-half RoPE; FLUX 3 video VAE, ``eps=1e-5`` |
 | `fused_complex_rope` | Triton | preserves CUDA complex64 multiply rounding for contiguous BSHD inputs; Qwen-Image 2.1 verifies its first call against eager |

@@ -15,6 +15,11 @@
 import torch
 from torch import nn
 
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import (
+    BitExactFusionGate,
+    fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact,
+    tensors_equal,
+)
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.models.dits.hidream_o1_image import (
     HiDreamO1ImageArchConfig,
     HiDreamO1ImageDitConfig,
@@ -38,6 +43,10 @@
 )
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits.base import BaseDiT
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import AttentionBackendEnum
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.logging_utils import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+_HIDREAM_ROPE = BitExactFusionGate("HiDream fused RoPE")
 
 # Checkpoint prefixes that carry no parameter of this model.
 UNUSED_CHECKPOINT_PREFIXES = ("model.visual.", "lm_head.")
@@ -214,7 +223,25 @@ def forward(
         v = v.reshape(batch_size, seq_len, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim)
 
         # cos/sin are [B, S, D]; broadcast over the head axis of [B, S, H, D].
-        q, k = qwen3_apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos.unsqueeze(2), sin.unsqueeze(2))
+        cos, sin = cos.unsqueeze(2), sin.unsqueeze(2)
+        if (
+            q.is_cuda
+            and q.dtype is torch.bfloat16
+            and q.is_contiguous()
+            and k.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            # Keep the BF16 rounding after each product in the eager RoPE.
+            q, k = _HIDREAM_ROPE.run(
+                lambda: (
+                    fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact(q, cos, sin),
+                    fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact(k, cos, sin),
+                ),
+                lambda: qwen3_apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin),
+                equal=tensors_equal,
+                logger=logger,
+            )
+        else:
+            q, k = qwen3_apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin)
 
         attn_output = self.attn(q, k, v, attn_mask=attention_mask)
         output, _ = self.o_proj(attn_output.reshape(batch_size, seq_len, -1))

@@ -2832,5 +2832,72 @@ def first_k(model, source, req):
         assert gone() is None
 
 
+@torch.inference_mode()
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["fused", "strided", "fp32", "mismatch"])
+def test_hidream_rope_dispatch_and_fallback(monkeypatch, mode):
+    """Preserve GQA and batch-specific tables, including the native fallback."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits import hidream_o1_image as hidream
+
+    gate = BitExactFusionGate("HiDream RoPE test")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(hidream, "_HIDREAM_ROPE", gate)
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(42)
+    dtype = torch.float32 if mode == "fp32" else torch.bfloat16
+    qkv = torch.randn(2, 17, 12 * 128, device="cuda", dtype=dtype, generator=generator)
+    angles = torch.randn(2, 17, 128, device="cuda", generator=generator)
+    cos, sin = angles.cos().to(dtype), angles.sin().to(dtype)
+    norm = (lambda x: x) if mode == "strided" else lambda x: x.contiguous()
+    captured = []
+
+    def attention(q, k, v, *, attn_mask):
+        captured.append((q, k, v))
+        return q
+
+    # Run the real attention forward; isolate its RoPE from projection weights
+    # and SDPA so a Q/K rounding mismatch cannot disappear in a later cast.
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_heads=8,
+        num_kv_heads=2,
+        head_dim=128,
+        q_size=8 * 128,
+        kv_size=2 * 128,
+        qkv_proj=lambda x: (x, None),
+        q_norm=norm,
+        k_norm=norm,
+        attn=attention,
+        o_proj=lambda x: (x, None),
+    )
+    fused = MagicMock(
+        side_effect=(
+            (lambda x, cos, sin: torch.zeros_like(x))
+            if mode == "mismatch"
+            else hidream.fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact
+        )
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(hidream, "fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact", fused)
+    mask = torch.zeros(1, 1, 17, 17, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    for x in (qkv, qkv * 2):
+        original = x.clone()
+        q, k, v = x.split([8 * 128, 2 * 128, 2 * 128], dim=-1)
+        expected_q, expected_k = hidream.qwen3_apply_rotary_pos_emb(
+            norm(q.reshape(2, 17, 8, 128)),
+            norm(k.reshape(2, 17, 2, 128)),
+            cos.unsqueeze(2),
+            sin.unsqueeze(2),
+        )
+        hidream.HiDreamO1Attention.forward(layer, x, cos, sin, mask)
+        actual_q, actual_k, actual_v = captured[-1]
+        assert torch.equal(actual_q, expected_q) and torch.equal(actual_k, expected_k)
+        assert torch.equal(actual_v, v.reshape(2, 17, 2, 128))
+        assert torch.equal(x, original)
+    assert (
+        fused.call_count == {"fused": 4, "strided": 0, "fp32": 0, "mismatch": 2}[mode]
+    )
+    assert gate.verified == (mode == "fused")
+    assert gate.disabled == (mode == "mismatch")
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
